items.title: Top 20+ Scholarships in Sweden for International Students
items.summary: ©iStock.com/cofkocof Until 2011, Sweden was one of the few countries in Europe where you could study for free . Students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland now pay application and tuition fees, which average around SEK 160,000 a year. To help with these costs, the Swedish Institute and almost every Swedish university offer scholarships in Sweden , and many of them cover tuition in full. Swedish Government Scholarships for International Students » Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (Sweden) The Swedish Institute’s Scholarship for Global Professionals supports professionals with work and leadership experience from eligible countries who want to study a full-time Master’s degree in Sweden. The scholarships go to outstanding candidates who cannot otherwise pay the tuition fee and the cost of living in Geneva. items.title: Ertegun Graduate Scholarships in the Humanities at University of Oxford
items.summary: University of Oxford Masters/PhD Degree Deadline: 5 Jan 2027 (most courses) Study in: UK Course starts October 2027 Brief description: The Mica and Ahmet Ertegun Graduate Scholarship Programme funds full-time graduate study in the humanities at the University of Oxford. It aims to choose the very best students who will go on to become leaders in their fields. The scholarships are highly competitive, with over 1,500 applicants for around 15 awards each year. items.title: Launching ANTART monthly gatherings!
items.summary: Dear ANTART Community, As the new convening team of the EASA Anthropology and the Arts (ANTART) Network, we would like to create more opportunities for our community to meet, exchange ideas, learn from one another, and get to know each other’s work. We are therefore excited to launch a new series of monthly online ANTART gatherings, taking place throughout the year, usually on the second or third Friday of each month at 10:00 AM (CEST). Rather than a formal seminar series, we envision these gatherings as an informal and welcoming space for sharing research, artistic practices, methods, works in progress, publications, projects, and questions related to anthropology and the arts. Each gathering will feature one or more short presentations, followed by time for conversation and exchange. items.title: Top 10+ International Scholarships offered by Global Organizations, Institutions, and Foundations
items.summary: ©iStock.com/Rawpixel Intergovernmental organizations, development banks and international foundations offer some of the best-known scholarships for international students. Many are fully funded, and many are aimed at students from developing countries who want to study abroad or in their own region. scholars4dev.com lists the top 10+ international scholarships offered by global organizations, institutions and foundations below. International Scholarships by Intergovernmental Organizations » Erasmus Mundus Scholarships (European Union) Funded by the European Union, Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters give full scholarships to students from all over the world, including a monthly allowance of €1,400, and students study in at least two countries during the programme. The scholarships cover a wide range of joint Master’s programmes in science, engineering, social sciences, humanities and business.

items.title: Harry Frank Guggenheim Emerging Scholar Awards for PhD Candidates
items.summary: Harry Frank Guggenheim Foundation PhD Degree Deadline: 31 Jan 2027 (annual) Study in: any Country Award starts 1 Sept 2027 Brief description: The Harry Frank Guggenheim Foundation (HFG) gives Emerging Scholar Awards to PhD candidates in their final year who are writing a dissertation on violence. The award helps them finish the dissertation on time. It does not pay for doctoral research itself, so it is meant for students whose fieldwork is already done. These awards were previously called the Harry Frank Guggenheim Dissertation Fellowships.
